rich_narrative.summary: Based in Illinois, Darul Qasim serves as an institute of higher Islamic learning dedicated to <cite id="1">facilitating knowledge derived from the Prophet Muhammad</cite>. The organization provides a structured curriculum including <cite id="4">Arabic language and religious education</cite> through various academic levels. In FY2024, the institute reported <cite id="1">total revenue of $2,696,418</cite>, which supported its mission of capacity building within the Muslim community. While the organization maintains <cite id="2">strong governance with 100% independent board members</cite>, its financial profile presents a balanced mix of high efficiency and significant capital retention. Specifically, the charity demonstrates <cite id="2">exceptional fundraising efficiency</cite>, spending only <cite id="2">$0.02 to raise every $1</cite> in FY2024. However, the <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 51.9%</cite> is notably lower than the <cite id="1">peer program ratio median of 89.8%</cite> for the education sector. This indicates that a substantial portion of annual spending is directed toward administrative or reserve functions rather than direct educational delivery. Furthermore, the organization experienced an <cite id="1">18% decline in revenue</cite> from the previous fiscal year, moving from <cite id="1">$3,290,091 in FY2023</cite> to the current FY2024 levels. Despite this contraction, Darul Qasim remains financially stable, holding <cite id="2">29.3 months of working capital</cite> in working capital. This level of reserves ensures long-term institutional survival but may raise questions for donors seeking immediate deployment of funds.
